small_guidance:
- Add larger BLOCK_K configs (128) with num_stages=3 to better amortize the K=8192 reduction; also try BLOCK_M=128/BLOCK_N=256/BLOCK_K=32 with num_warps=8/num_stages=4 — for M=N=2048 the dominant cost is the K-loop and wider BLOCK_K reduces loop trip count.
- Drop masking on the K dimension inside the hot loop: K=8192 is divisible by all candidate BLOCK_K values, so replace the masked `tl.load` with unmasked loads (still mask M/N edges) to cut predicate overhead.
- Tighten the autotune config list to 3-4 most promising entries (e.g. 128x256x64/w8/s3, 256x128x64/w8/s4, 128x128x64/w8/s3) to reduce tuning noise and let the warmup converge to the true best.
large_guidance:
- Switch to a split-K or persistent-kernel GEMM: with M=N=2048 there are only 64-256 output tiles depending on block size, which underfills the 128 SMs on the 4090. A persistent kernel with one program per SM walking a tile queue, or a split-K reduction over the K=8192 axis, would expose more parallelism.
- Consider TF32 (`tl.dot(..., allow_tf32=True)`) or fp16 accumulation path; the 4090 has much higher tensor-core throughput on TF32/FP16 than FP32, and the loose 5e-2 tolerance easily accommodates TF32 mantissa loss.
- Pre-transpose the weight into a (K, N) contiguous buffer at __init__ so stride_wk=N (contiguous along N for inner load) — currently stride_wk=1 means the N-axis load is strided by K=8192, which hurts coalescing on the B operand inside `tl.dot`.
